title: Snoozer's background and fingerpicking style
summary: He gives Snoozer's Bogalusa origins and his speed, finger picking and ballads.

blocks.x: Can you tell a bit more about him? He came from... Bogalooza. Was he born over that way?
Yeah, he was born and raised there, yeah. He's still got brothers over there.

He's got a brother that's a barber. He's got a barber shop over there. In Bogalooza. You never heard anything like it, Bill. I've heard a lot of guitar players. I've heard Lang and all those, Segovia. But nobody played like Snooza. The guy was just, he was out of the world.
Did he ever play here in the city with many of the bands?

Oh, he played, he played. Not working, not studying, but sit in. He used to come over here all the time. He would, in fact, he'd come over and he'd stay over maybe a month, two months. He used to room here on magazine. Whenever he'd come in town, he used to room right here on magazine and first. Because that's where we went and got him to bring him down there to hear white. We thought he'd have his guitar and his fiddle. He only played fiddle, too. But he didn't have his instruments with him. And his mother and his aunt was with him at that time. And they were living right here at first in magazine. Or second in magazine. But if you didn't hear him, I don't know how. I never have heard the tapes that Johnny's got.
I don't see how they could do him justice.
They probably don't do him justice.
I don't think they could do him justice.
Did he play with a picker with his finger or both?

Both. And he played jazz. He played wonderful jazz. And fast. He was the fastest man picking that I ever heard in my life. I mean, he'd make all these guys sound like they're playing waltzes. You know, that's how fast he was. And like I tell you, he used to do that and just pick with this hand here. And play the damn best thing. Yeah, boy. Then he'd turn right around and he'd play with the pick. And he'd play some beautiful things like Mighty Like a Rose and those kind of things, you know. Coquette. And play a ballad. And play, oh, most beautiful.
I noticed you were showing him as if they were left-handed. I was wondering if he were. No, no. That's I am. No, no.
